# Ergonomics: verified primary sources

Checked **17 Sep 2026** using public pages only. No repository or user data was transmitted. WAI Understanding pages explain WCAG criteria; they are not independent conformance certification. US government guidance is jurisdiction-specific, not an Indian dimensional preset.

## W3C/WAI: Understanding SC 2.5.7, Dragging Movements
- URL: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html
- Checked: 17 Sep 2026.
- Establishes: dragging functionality generally needs a single-pointer alternative that does not require dragging; keyboard equivalence alone does not meet this separate requirement. Clickable choices or numeric controls can provide alternatives.
- Does not establish: that a particular HomePlanner widget conforms, that a keyboard-only fallback is sufficient, or that UI accessibility proves a physically accessible layout.

## W3C/WAI: Understanding SC 2.1.1, Keyboard
- URL: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html
- Checked: 17 Sep 2026.
- Establishes: keyboard operation should cover functions whose result does not inherently depend on the input path; positioning, resizing and straight-line drawing are not automatically exempt. Platform conventions support discoverable operation.
- Does not establish: complete WCAG compliance, tested screen-reader support, or permission to override text-entry shortcuts. Focus visibility, cancellation and native field behaviour still need separate examination.

## US Access Board: Entrances, Doors and Gates
- URL: https://www.access-board.gov/ada/guides/chapter-4-entrances-doors-and-gates/
- Checked: 17 Sep 2026; guide to the ADA Standards, including §404.
- Establishes: clear opening is measured with the operating door and stop/leaf relationship, not simply nominal leaf width. Maneuvering space depends on approach, swing and other conditions; entrance landings need coordinated review.
- Does not establish: ADA applicability to every dwelling, equivalent Indian rules, a universal frame deduction, or a compliant stair/lift/escape route. Do not transplant dimensions without confirming scope and governing edition.

## US Access Board: Operable Parts
- URL: https://www.access-board.gov/ada/guides/chapter-3-operable-parts/
- Checked: 17 Sep 2026; guide discusses ADA §§205, 308 and 309.
- Establishes: reach concerns the operable portion and its approach space; forward/side approach, obstructions and knee/toe space change the assessment. User operation is more than plan-footprint non-overlap.
- Does not establish: an individual user's clinical needs, universal ergonomic dimensions, a local electrical installation rule or verified reach from an unspecified symbol height. User/context dimensions and applicable authority remain necessary.
